title: Chronic kidney disease: diet and monitoring
what: In chronic kidney disease, the kidneys clean the blood less well. Diet, blood pressure, and regular tests help slow the disease.
why: If a doctor found chronic kidney disease, often with diabetes or high blood pressure.
duration: tests are usually done every few months
tell_doctor: All medicines and supplements, since some harm the kidneys
If you have swelling, pass little urine, or its color changed
If you are going for a test with contrast

prepare.title: Painkillers
prepare.text: Do not take painkillers or herbs without asking your doctor, since some harm the kidneys.

prepare.title: Diet
prepare.text: How much salt, protein, potassium, and fluid is allowed, your doctor will say. It depends on the stage.

prepare.title: Blood pressure and sugar
prepare.text: Keep them at the numbers your doctor gave you.

steps: Less salt: do not add salt at the table and avoid sausages, canned food, and chips
Protein in the amount your doctor prescribed
If your doctor limited potassium, find out which foods have a lot of it
Drink as much fluid as your doctor says
Measure your blood pressure and write it down
Have blood and urine tests on schedule
feel: In the early stages, often nothing bothers you
Later there may be weakness, itching, or swelling, so tell your doctor
after: Show your test results to your doctor
Tell every doctor that you have kidney disease
Ask about the vaccines you need
red_flags: Very little urine or none for almost a day: see a doctor urgently
Severe shortness of breath or growing swelling: call emergency services
Severe weakness or skipped heartbeats: call emergency services

faq.a: Often it can be slowed. The earlier treatment starts, the better.

faq.q: Should I drink a lot of water?
faq.a: Not always. At some stages, water is limited instead. Ask your doctor.

reminders.text: Kidney tests tomorrow. Bring the referral and your blood pressure diary.
